hits.snippet: AI-powered materials discovery startup Discovered Materials has raised $9 Mn (about ₹85.9 Cr) in a seed funding round led by Lightspeed India Partners. # Discovered Materials Closes $9M Seed Round to Accelerate the Adoption of New Materials for Semiconductor Chips

Founders of Discovered Materials. Akash (left) and Advaith (right)

Business Wire

Mon, August 10, 2026 at 6:00 AM MST 3 min read

[](https://s.yimg.
com/lo/mysterio/api/008F9741B30450976399A4FD249730BBA11FE769522CF430C79AC8DFE00F7ED5/subgraphmysterio/resizefit_w960;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fbusiness-wire.com%2Ff139d742cb98fe8ac116f47122acc192)

_Funding round led by Lightspeed will scale the company's AI agents, compressing years of materials R&D and shrinking the lab-to-fab timeline_

**SAN FRANCISCO, August 10, 2026** \--( [BUSINESS WIRE](https://www.businesswire.com) )--Today, Discovered Materials, a company building AI agents that discover and accelerate the adoption of new materials for semiconductor chips, announces a $9M seed round. They also released hundreds of new materials discovered by frontier AI models, along with [Material Discovery](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fdiscoveredmaterials.com%2Fresearch%2Fmaterial-discovery-bench.
html&esheet=54586004&newsitemid=20260810167426&lan=en-US&anchor=Material+Discovery&index=1&md5=d13d4f8eca4480b59d5ce65464f39882) [Bench](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fdiscoveredmaterials.com%2Fresearch%2Fmaterial-discovery-bench.html&esheet=54586004&newsitemid=20260810167426&lan=en-US&anchor=Bench&index=2&md5=3e96e7da82890d447f5d309a59efbfc7) \- the first benchmark for agentic materials discovery on real-world semiconductor chip problems.

The round is led by Lightspeed India Partners, with participation from Y Combinator and Peak XV Partners, and angel investors including Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram and Thariq Shihipar. The funding will accelerate the company's mission: making new materials discovery fast enough to keep pace with AI's demand for compute.

"AI is creating unprecedented demand for better chips, but progress is increasingly constrained by how slowly new materials reach production.

excerpts:
# Discovered Materials Raises $9 Million Seed Funding To Accelerate AI-Powered Semiconductor Materials Discovery

By Amit Chowdhry Aug 10, 2026

[Pulse 2.0](https://pulse2.com "Pulse 2.0")

Discovered Materials Raises $9 Million Seed Funding To Accelerate AI-Powered Semiconductor Materials Discovery

[Follow Pulse 2.0 on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/pulse2news)

Discovered Materials has raised $9 million in seed funding to expand its use of AI agents for discovering and accelerating the adoption of new materials used in semiconductor chips. The round was led by Lightspeed India Partners, with participation from Y Combinator and Peak XV Partners. Angel investors including Paul Graham, Gokul Rajaram and Thariq Shihipar also participated.

Discovered Materials is developing AI agents designed to compress semiconductor materials research timelines by combining simulation, synthesis and experimental validation.

...

Discovered Materials also introduced Material Discovery Bench, which it describes as the first benchmark for agentic materials discovery focused on real-world semiconductor problems. The benchmark was developed with experts from industry and academia and is designed to track the performance of frontier models.

The company plans to continue developing evaluation systems that test AI-discovered materials through both simulation and physical experiments.

Discovered Materials said that over the past three months, it has developed new thermal materials that match the performance of products that major chemical companies took years to develop.

The company was co-founded by Advaith Sridhar and Akash Ramdas, who met more than a decade ago at IIT Madras.

Ramdas holds a Ph.D. in materials science from Stanford University and has spent approximately 11 years researching semiconductor materials.

...

In the last 3 months, we have made new thermal materials that match the performance of products that the world’s largest chemical companies took years to develop.”_

**Akash Ramdas, Co-Founder of Discovered Materials**
